headline: Lanai Planning Commission

meeting.summary: The commission elected officers, found a hotel restaurant renovation exempt from a coastal-zone permit, and heard training on planning and open-meetings law.
meeting.recap: New commissioner David DeLeon introduced himself to the commission.[[0:02:32]] Commissioners elected a fellow commissioner as vice chair by a show of hands.[[0:05:14]] The chair agreed to serve another year after no one else volunteered.[[0:07:50]] The commission unanimously agreed that planned renovations at an existing hotel restaurant do not need a special management area permit (a coastal-zone permit).[[0:20:42]] Planning staff gave commissioners an orientation training.[[0:21:52]] A county lawyer trained commissioners on the Sunshine Law, which is the state's open meetings law.[[1:07:19]] The lawyer asked commissioners to turn in their financial disclosures, which are required before they can vote.[[1:28:13]] The chair said two Lānaʻi residents have been interviewed for open commission seats.[[2:11:28]] The chair said that for terms ending in March 2027, the nominations board must get applications by December 31st.[[2:12:43]] Staff said the planning director allows in-person meetings but does not want staff to stay overnight.[[2:14:27]] The chair asked staff to get the director's position on hybrid meetings, part in person and part online.[[2:26:47]] Staff said new rules letting the commission review SMA minor permits await the mayor's approval.[[2:32:05]] Staff said there are no agenda items yet for the June 17th meeting.[[2:33:29]]
decided: Commissioners elected a fellow commissioner as vice chair for the next year.
Commissioners unanimously re-elected the chair for another year.
The commission agreed with the planning department that renovations at an existing hotel restaurant are exempt from needing a special management area permit.
meeting.next: Staff will ask that a copy of the orientation presentation be sent directly to the new commissioner. The county lawyer said he would look into an earlier legal opinion the chair mentioned on commissioner conflicts of interest. The chair said the mayor's office plans to send the two residents' names to the County Council for approval. Staff will ask the planning director why she does not want overnight stays and what her position is on hybrid meetings. The planning department will bring any SMA minor permit to the commission even before the new rules are signed.
